subject: Cost & Latency Forensics Playbook — tenant route anomaly
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-04-07T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Spike last night on /v1/chat -> can we build a forensics playbook?

Hey Dylan,

Acme hit a big tenant-only cost/latency spike on /v1/chat yesterday evening (their traffic pattern shows sudden long-tail token growth). CS asked for a clear, repeatable post-mortem + runbook we can hand to their ops team and to on-call.

What I'm imagining: a short (1) checklist for immediate mitigation (rate limits, fallback model, isolate tenant), (2) a triage worksheet for engineers (sequence length distribution, KV cache hit/miss, batching changes, quantization variant in use), and (3) a packet/trace collection template so customers can send us useful artifacts without exposing secret data.

I started a skeleton in the attached forensics_template.xlsx and grabbed a trace screenshot (spike_trace_2028-04-06.png). Can you take point on turning this into a product-facing playbook with concrete console actions (per-route dashboards, an exportable trace link, one-click fallback to a cheaper model)? Grace — can you flag any console UX constraints (what tile/API we can expose quickly)?

Thanks — Camila

Camila Reyes
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
camila.reyes@redwood.com

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-04-07T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Spike last night on /v1/chat -> can we build a forensics playbook?

Thanks for pulling this together, Camila. I'm happy to own the playbook doc and coordinate with product/infra. Quick notes: 

- We need a short-term mitigation checklist that CS can execute from the console without engineering involvement (rate-limit toggle, model variant pin, tenant throttling).
- For triage we should capture: request histograms by minute, percentile token lengths, KV cache hit rate, batch sizes, model variant and quantization, and any fallback events.
- The trace screenshot looks like a KV cache miss storm followed by a large batching latency outlier. We'll confirm with Karthik.

Karthik — can you propose a minimal set of telemetry signals we can reliably surface in the console within two sprints? Grace — if we wanted a one-click "fall back to compatible model (cheaper)" action, what permissions & UI surface do we need? Also, what's the fastest way to let a CS rep export sanitized traces to attach to a support ticket (prefer a zip that strips PII)?

I'll work the doc and open a short RFC for product review.

— Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Product Manager, Observability — Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-04-07T14:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Spike last night on /v1/chat -> can we build a forensics playbook?

Quick technical readout after a skim of the sample_kv_dump.jsonl and the trace:

1) Root signals to include (minimal):
   - per-route P50/P95/P99 latency (tokenization + generation split)
   - sequence-length heatmap (bucketed: 0-64,65-256,257-1024,>1024)
   - KV cache hit ratio over 1h/6h windows
   - per-tenant batching histogram (requests per batch)
   - model variant + quantization flag (string) and whether fallback occurred
   - number of failed decodes / safety hits (if present)

2) For rapid console work: we can add a "Forensics" tab on the route detail page that queries existing traces and a short-lived sanitized export job. Implementation notes:
   - Export job should run server-side, redact potential PII (input/text fields) via heuristic removal, and produce a staged S3 zip with trace.jsonl + sampled_kv.jsonl + a small metrics.csv. TTL 24 hours.
   - One-click fallback can be a route action that switches the route's model variant to a chosen compatible target. We already have model pin API; surface it as an "emergency fallback" with audit logging and rollback.

3) Quick mitigations CS can do via console (no infra sprint):
   - toggle per-route throttle (requests/sec cap)
   - enable disabled-caching flag (if small tenant causing cache thrash)
   - temporarily reduce max output tokens or switch to a cheaper compatible model

I'll sketch a minimal telemetry schema and example queries by EOD tomorrow. If we commit to the export job approach, I can nominate the minimal fields to capture and a sample redact list.

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Elena Suarez <elena@acme-data.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
Cc: ops-team@acme-data.com
Date: 2028-04-09T15:43:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Spike last night on /v1/chat -> can we build a forensics playbook?

Appreciate the quick turnaround and the proposed playbook approach. A few priorities from our side:

- We need a sanitized export we can give to our internal SREs — ideally an S3 link we can pull into our incident playbook.
- The one-click fallback is high priority; during the spike we had to manually update client-side configs which took too long.
- Please include a decision matrix in the playbook: when to throttle vs when to fallback vs when to escalate to Redwood infra for kernel-level investigation.

Attached the failing request IDs we captured in case they are useful (referenced in sample_kv_dump.jsonl). Happy to jump on a 30 min sync if helpful.

Thanks — Elena
Elena Suarez
Head of Platform Ops, Acme Data
